extracted.intended_audience: third parties (and their practitioners) preparing preissuance submissions under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) / 37 CFR 1.290 (e.g., patent practitioners, attorneys, agents, members of the public submitting prior art)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and filing third-party preissuance submissions under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and 37 CFR 1.290, including document identification, copies, translations, concise descriptions of relevance, statements, and fee rules. Targets preparation of compliant submissions that can be entered into a patent application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(e)(1) requires that each U.S. patent be identified by patent number, first named inventor, and issue date. 37 CFR 1.290(e)(2) requires that each U.S. patent application publication be identified by patent application publication number, first named inventor, and publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification information aids in locating items if document numbers are in error (e.g., transposed). When using the USPTO Web-based interface it will automatically generate a document list in accordance with these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of foreign patents and published foreign patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(e)(3) requires that each foreign patent or published foreign patent application be identified by the country or patent office that issued or published the document; the applicant, patentee, or first named inventor; an appropriate document number; and the publication date indicated on the patent or published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule permits identification by applicant or patentee in addition to the first named inventor to provide flexibility and to help identify items if the document number is wrong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of non-patent publications
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(e)(4) requires that each non-patent publication be identified by author (if any), title, pages being submitted, publication date, and where available, publisher and place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.290(e)(4) does not preclude providing additional information (e.g., journal title and volume/issue). For internet sources, provide the URL of the web page that is the source and, when obtained from an archive, provide both the archived page URL and the source website URL (example format shown in MPEP). Publisher/place may be omitted if unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide evidence when no publication date is known
rubrics_metrics.description: If no publication date is known for a non-patent publication, the third party must provide evidence of publication and at least a date of retrieval or a time frame when the document was available as a publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence can include affidavits, declarations, website printouts showing retrieval date, screenshots, emails showing distribution, or trade show distribution statements. See the Evidence of Publication section for examples and formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise description of relevance required for each listed item
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(d)(2) requires a concise description of the asserted relevance of each item identified in the document list (as required by 35 U.S.C. 122(e)(2)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise description of relevance is a statement of facts regarding the submitted evidence and will not be treated as evidence. It should explain how the item is potentially relevant to examination and may be narrative or a claim chart. It is more effective when it points out the relevant pages, lines, figures, or paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format options for concise description of relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The concise description may be presented in any format that best explains relevance, such as narrative description or a claim chart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing electronically, the Web interface includes a field for the concise description; a third party may upload a separate paper in lieu of entering text in the field. When filing on paper, provide the concise description as a separate paper for each item (do not combine descriptions for many items into one paper) and prominently identify the item to which the description pertains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content limits for concise description of relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: At a minimum, a concise description must be more than a bare statement that the document is relevant (e.g., 'Document 1 is relevant' is insufficient). A copy merely annotated or highlighted will not be deemed a proper concise description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid verbosity; be focused. A concise description that includes a short field-intro plus a claim chart mapping document portions to claim elements is likely acceptable. Descriptions that merely repeat information in a claim chart or that approach the length of the documents themselves are not likely to be considered 'concise.' Descriptions that appear to be mere form paragraphs opposing a general class of inventions are non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction against third-party participation in prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: The concise description of relevance must not permit third-party participation in prosecution; it is limited to factual description of a document's relevance and must not rise to the level of a protest under 37 CFR 1.291.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit arguments against patentability, propose rejections, or set forth conclusions that claims are unpatentable in the concise description. Contrast: protests under 1.291 may include arguments; concise descriptions under 122(e) may not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of compliant versus non-compliant concise descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP provides narrative and claim-chart examples showing compliant content (factual mappings to claim elements, pointing to specific pages/lines/figures) and non-compliant content (statements asserting obviousness or that a claim is unpatentable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the examples as templates: indicate which claim elements are disclosed by which parts of a publication and cite precise pages/lines/figures. Avoid bolded-style argument language that concludes unpatentability or obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required for submitted items
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(d)(3) requires submission of a legible copy of each item identified in the document list other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications (which need not be submitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies submitted in color will be scanned into black and white. No CDs or other electronic media accepted for paper filings; electronic uploads permitted via the Web interface. If only a portion of a document is listed, submit a copy of that portion and not the entire document, but include identifying pages (cover, title page, copyright page) for identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying labels and organization as a best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether filing on paper or electronically, include an identifying label for each item in the document list and place that label on the concise description, on the copy of the item, and on the translation so screeners and examiners can readily identify correspondences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice facilitates faster screening and accurate entry into the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of images and visibility in Public PAIR
rubrics_metrics.description: Images of non-patent literature cited in a compliant third-party submission will not be available for viewing or downloading through Public PAIR; the Office separates the document list (bibliographic info) from the copies so bibliographic data will be visible in Public PAIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office treats document entry similarly to how IDS submissions are entered under 37 CFR 1.98.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non-English items
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(d)(4) requires an English language translation of any non-English language item identified in the document list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reliable machine translation is acceptable and need not be certified. If only a portion of a non-English document is listed, submit a copy and translation of only that portion (do not submit a translation of the entire document).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(d)(5)(i) requires a statement that the party making the submission is not an individual who has a duty to disclose under 37 CFR 1.56. 37 CFR 1.290(d)(5)(ii) requires a statement that the submission complies with 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and 37 CFR 1.290. Submissions must be signed by the submitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/429 and the Web interface include required statements. The Office will not entertain challenges to the accuracy of such statements; false statements may be penalized under 18 U.S.C. 1001. The submitter must sign (cannot remain anonymous), though the real party in interest may remain anonymous by using another person to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement and item-counting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(f) requires payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(o) for every ten items or fraction thereof listed in the document list, except where the submission qualifies for the fee exemption under 37 CFR 1.290(g). The Office determines item count based on the 1.290(d)(1) document list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications identified in the document list count toward the item count even if copies are not submitted. If only a portion of a publication is identified, that portion counts as one item. Multiple publications from the same website each count as separate items. Payment methods differ for electronic and paper filing (credit card, deposit account, EFT for electronic; check, money order, credit card, deposit account for paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee exemption under 37 CFR 1.290(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.290(g) provides an exemption from the fee requirement where the submission lists three or fewer total items and is the first third-party submission by that third party (or a party in privity) in a given application, subject to a required 'first and only' statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee-exempt submission must be accompanied by a statement that, after reasonable inquiry, the submission is the first and only third-party submission by the third party or a party in privity in the application. Third parties are not required to use the exemption and may elect to pay instead. If subsequent submissions are made, they are subject to fees. Resubmissions after non-compliance generally require payment unless prior fee application is accepted at the Office's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity discount and micro entity ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A small entity discount is available for third-party submissions where applicable; micro entity discount is not available for third-party submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To claim small entity when filing on paper, select the small entity box on form PTO/SB/429 (or equivalent) and pay the reduced fee. Selecting the small entity box asserts that the party qualifies as a small entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission after finding of non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third-party submission is found non-compliant, the third party may correct and resubmit provided the statutory filing period remains open; the resubmission must be a new complete submission and the appropriate fee must accompany the resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not accept amendments to the non-compliant submission. If the original non-compliant submission included proper fee, the filer may request that the Office apply the previously-paid fee to the resubmission; this is at the Office's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible types of submitted information (what counts as a 'printed publication')
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions under 35 U.S.C. 122(e)(1) and 37 CFR 1.290(a) are limited to patents, published patent applications, and other printed publications that qualify as publications (e.g., published articles, Office actions issued in published applications, communications from foreign patent offices issued in published applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials that do not qualify as publications (e.g., items subject to protective orders, trade secrets, unpublished internal corporate documents, non-widely-disseminated emails) must not be submitted. Visual outputs (software/video) must be reduced to writing (e.g., screenshots). Physical samples must not be submitted; they will be discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance screening and consequence of non-publication findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions will be reviewed for compliance before being forwarded to an examiner. If any submitted document appears not to be a publication on its face, the entire submission will be found non-compliant and will not be entered into the file or considered by the examiner and will be discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant has evidence that a submitted document is not a publication, the applicant may challenge the Office's determination (for example, in response to a rejection applying the questioned document).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of publication formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence supporting that an item is a publication (when needed) must be specific to the document(s) submitted and will be evaluated for authenticity and persuasiveness. Affidavits/declarations must comply with the Office's formal requirements and the affiant/declarant must have personal knowledge of the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations should be limited to facts establishing why the submitted document qualifies as a publication and not be used to place extraneous information before the examiner. Examples: employee declaration of distribution at a trade show, emails showing public dissemination, website printouts/snapshots with retrieval dates, archived web page URLs with retrieval dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on inserting unpublished materials into concise descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party submissions that include unpublished materials as attachments to or inserted into the text of a concise description of relevance for a listed publication will be found non-compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish to rely on an additional published source to illustrate a point, that source itself must be listed and submitted for consideration; do not insert unpublished images or materials into the concise description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web-archive citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When a publication is obtained from a website that archives web pages, include both the URL of the archived web page submitted and the URL of the website from which the archived copy was obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format provided in MPEP shows how to list archived page URL and retrieval date alongside the source site URL for identification.
